$comment: INC-0924 — the Encrypted-mode row, and the one-time migration of the preference behind it.
There is no web consumer and there must not be one: this table is about an ANDROID control over an
ANDROID-local preference (E2eSettings C-1: the setting is per-device and the server never gets a vote).
The file lives in tests/ beside the cross-surface vectors so the android lane reads its fixtures from
one place, not to imply a second implementation exists.
THE INCIDENT THIS FILE EXISTS FOR. Until this build forState returned `checked = enabled && checkedPref`,
so a stored ON was drawn as OFF in every state except PEER_SUPPORTED. The masked value was the SAME
value E2eNegotiation.decide() reads at Accept, so a phone sitting in the lobby showed an OFF switch and
then forced a SAS-blocking encrypted pair: 'the phone automatically is pushing encrypted mode even
though it's not toggled on' (Dennis, 2026-09-24, phone v65 1.0.41). Every `checked` below is therefore
EXACTLY `checkedPref` — that is the assertion, not an accident of the table.
`subLine` names the extra line the row shows underneath the capability reason, or null. It exists so
that un-masking the switch does not produce a control that is ON, grey and unexplained.
